utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case IT-08-91-T, the Prosecutor versus Mico Stanisic and Stojan Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Good morning to everyone. May we have the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Matthew Olmsted, Joanna Korner, and Crispian Smith for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Slobodan Zecevic, Slobodan Cvijetic, and Eugene O'Sullivan appearing for Stanisic Defence this morning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. For Zupljanin Defence, Igor Pantelic, Dragan Krgovic, and Jason Antley.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Good morning to you, Mr. Radulovic. I remind you you're still on your oath. Yes, Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Radulovic.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I will try briefly to go through some of the topics so that you would be able to go home tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Let us get back to a topic you were asked about by Judge Harhoff yesterday when he was asking you about your work for the state security of Serbia. While you were working for that service, you believed you were working in the interests of the service and the Serbian People?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: There was no awareness of you assisting a Greater Serbia in your preparing of reports and doing your work, had nothing to do with your beliefs as a human being and as a professional?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. Although I do not believe very much in various statements about Greater Serbia because when compared to Russia or Canada, one realises Serbia is a very small country both by the number of inhabitants and its territory. It's among the smaller countries of the world. Now, ideas of some individuals who believe they are greater Greater Serbia, Greater Croatia, Greater Bosnia and Herzegovina, I see them as fanatics.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And all your work -- or all the work that is in the interest of the Serbian People at the time doesn't necessarily mean that you're backing the great Serbian ideas or that you have discriminatory intentions?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I differentiate between patriotism, jingoism, extreme nationalism, and so on. To be a patriot doesn't mean one is an extreme nationalist or jingoist. One can love his own country without hating other people. People -- Holland is a very good example of that. There are all sorts of people living here and yet they tolerate each other in every aspect of their being.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: When the Prosecutor presented to you an article about a press conference during which Mr. Zupljanin stated that he would not be carrying out orders by the MUP of Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina that are contrary to the interests of the Serbian People, that meant that he would not be obeying and implementing decisions that are harmful to the country, and all these things were already under way, have been started by the republican MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: I object to that question. I mean, it's really trying to get into the head of Mr. Zupljanin and what he made by a statement he made to the press, and I think that this witness also testified that he wasn't at the press conference even. So I'm not sure that's an appropriate question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, precisely because of this statement by the Prosecutor, namely, I objected earlier when the Prosecutor tried to link up the press conference and some interest. There were claims -- I made the claim that this was a leading question, and what I'm asking the witness now is to tell me how he understood the article, because we've heard in the direct examination his views on the article; and so this is directly linked up with the questions put by the Prosecutor at the time the Prosecutor was presenting the opposing option.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Should I answer the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's wait for the Trial Chamber to make a ruling.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Mr. Krgovic, how are we assisted by the witness's impression, understanding, whatever, of an article relating to an event at which he was not present? Which I understand to be the essence of Mr. Olmsted's objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, my colleague from the Prosecution asked the witness how did this statement by Stojan Zupljanin influence the behaviour of Muslim members of MUP -- MUP of the Bosnia-Herzegovina at the time. He linked this up with another document and asked the witness to comment on the -- on the statement made by Mr. Zupljanin. I objected to that because the Prosecutor gave him a suggestion as to what the answer might be, and what I'm asking the witness now is to hear his understanding of the statement, how he understood this statement, and how was it implemented.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In his view --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Sorry, could you remind me as to how the objection was resolved by the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Trial Chamber denied my objection and told the witness to answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And -- and the Prosecutor is now objecting to the same approach that they had before.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Your Honours, that's a misrepresentation of what happened. The Prosecution linked this press release or this article in the newspaper to one of the Mr. Radulovic's Milos reports, and that's all we did. We didn't ask him to comment on any of the things that Mr. Krgovic is suggesting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, let's move on. I don't see how we would be assisted by the witness's opinion on this. It's too disconnected.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: We'll move to a different topic. During your direct testimony, you discussed your contact and meetings -- contacts and meetings with Mr. Zupljanin. As far as I understood your testimony, you didn't have many opportunities to meet with Mr. Zupljanin. It was only on several occasions that you met with him, and the Prosecutor asked you about them. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. As far as I remember, I responded that I had direct conversations with Mr. Stojan Zupljanin in relation to five or six incidents, and I added that I may have had discussion about the same incident -- I had several discussions about the same with him, but I certainly did not have an opportunity to have daily conversations with him and definitely not about every dispatch or report I submitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And every time you drew attention of Mr. Zupljanin to some trend or something else that caused you a concern, Mr. Zupljanin always responded either immediately or after a short period.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Shall I be brief?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The briefest answer would be, Your statement is correct. But I believe I should add that first such response of his was in relation to Doboj, where, after about two days, members of the special unit were withdrawn, that he reacted to cases related to Keraterm, Omarska, Kotor Varos, Koricanske Stene, by forming a commission which carried out an on-site investigation. I stated this clearly. That's the state of fact. I think it be superfluous for me to give more explanations of our contacts related to individual incidents mentioned. I even mentioned this case at the cross-roads of Teslic, Prnjavor, and Doboj roads, when contact was established through hand-held radio station. At the time we didn't have mobile phones. And I also told you what his response was. He said that at any cost, crime or massacre must be prevented, and that on the basis of my very brief radio reporting. His answer was as I've just told you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I remember, you said that he told you that an assistant is coming from Prnjavor, that you should prevent it at any cost, and then the people in question boarded a bus and departed from there.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. You elaborated a bit on what I just told you about the incident. But, yes, that's correct. None of the persons who were at the location suffered any consequences. The only problem was the time they spent waiting there during which they must have been afraid for their lives.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise, in your last answer when you were mentioning the cases where Mr. Zupljanin reacted to your suggestions, in the transcript we don't see mention of Koricanske Stene. It's page 6, line 8. Apart from the responses you saw or knew about, let me show you a document that shows other reactions of Mr. Zupljanin to information received from you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So could we please have P198 put up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, tab number, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's Zupljanin Defence binder, tab 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, P198. 65 ter 921, if that's of any assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, P160.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You said that when you provided reports about the situation in Prijedor, whenever you had an opportunity, you'd tell Zupljanin about some events, trends, and your concern. You would, for instance, mention elements of the crime who were the victims, all these things about victims, mode of perpetration. These things were not something that you at the time. You just gave him a general picture?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And essence of your report concerning the camps was that people were put at two locations, you mentioned which ones, that the conditions there were poor, that some of the individuals guarding them are not abiding by the norms of the international humanitarian law, that the military and Crisis Staff are putting in huge numbers of people into spaces that cannot fit them, and that was the essence of your report to Zupljanin?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. I would add also that in Omarska I'd seen some dead bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Would you please look at this brief analysis from July 1992. It was a meeting of the MUP officials held in Belgrade, and all leading officials of MUP were present there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have page 5 in the B/C/S version; page 8 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: On the Serb part, there -- present are Mico Stanisic, Mr. Skipina, all minister assistants, all chiefs of various centres. We can see Mr. Zupljanin speaking here. Petar Mihajlovic is here on behalf of the -- of the Serbian -- from Serbia authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have page 5 in Serbian version. Page 8 in the English version, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Please have a look at paragraph 2 where Mr. Zupljanin says: "The army and Crisis Staffs," that is to say the War Presidencies, "request that as many members of the Muslim population should be collected and such undefined camps are then left for the MUP organs. The conditions in these camps are bad. There's no food. Some individuals do not respect international norms because such collection centres, among other things, are not adequate or there are some other reasons." In essence, let us not go into details. That was your information, is that correct, and it reflected the situation that you saw and reported about it. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can recognise it, and it's almost a perfect match.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And if you know that after this, the Ministry of the Interior initiated before the Ministry of the Interior of Republika Srpska that Keraterm and Omarska should be disbanded later on Trnopolje as well. Are you familiar with that?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, I am familiar with that. But I wish to warn you that I am not familiar with all activities of Mr. Stojan Zupljanin, and I want to distance myself from what he was doing in context with his superiors and with the political organs at the level of Banja Luka and Republika Srpska as a whole. So please place me within my own context, and that means in the intelligence activities which had nothing to do with monitoring this type of Stojan Zupljanin's active, nor did it have anything to do with his activities in relation with reporting to political and other structures at the level of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Maybe my question was imprecise. I just wanted to ask you whether you know that after this period of time, according to the information you had, these centres were disbanded. I mean the ones in Omarska and in Keraterm.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I remember, you also said that after the first disbelief which Mr. Zupljanin expressed, he called for you a few days later and told you that you were right in relation to these incidents. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The Prosecutor showed you a video-clip --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I'm referring to the events in Prijedor, and you also had that in mind when you answered; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's just what I had in mind. But I have to tell you that he had a similar comment about the incidents in Doboj.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The Prosecutor showed you a video-clip from the 30th of July, 1992, where you had the occasion to see certain people, and I will now show you a document which is a summary of the meeting and also contains some of the information that you talked about. So I will read to you some sections of this document to see whether this matches the situation that existed in the Banja Luka region at the time and the information that you had at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So could we please see in e-court Exhibit 2D25.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Krgovic, could I add something, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure what Mr. Simo Drljaca showed Stojan Zupljanin and the commission which went to Prijedor in relation with Keraterm, Omarska, and Trnopolje. You're probably aware that something can be portrayed as being nice or camouflage, so to speak, so that people who are coming from somewhere else see something else than what is the reality. I'm convinced, even though I do not have any operative information, that Simo Drljaca presented to them a situation different than the actual one. I wish to be completely sincere about this. However, I do believe that he saw the situation, that Vojin Bera saw the situation as it was. I know that, and I checked that. Vojin Bera and also others who visited Omarska and Keraterm. I also remember a colleague of mine from the public security service, Mr. Obrad Despotovic, who informed me in detail about what was going on in Omarska, and he did that even before I visited Omarska for the first time. So considering that, I believe that those who were in charge of investigations did not report to the leadership in a timely fashion, neither the state or public security service leaderships. Consequently, the top officials of the Ministry of Interior of Republika Srpska could not receive adequate reports and neither could the political leadership. So, to sum it up, there were attempts to conceal the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Radulovic, can I just follow up on this answer that you just gave to Mr. Krgovic because it wasn't clear to me whether -- what Vojin Bera said to Zupljanin. Did Bera try to give to Zupljanin a true picture of how things were, or did he also seek to cover it up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I am very clear. He was not trying to do that, but he hashed it up. The events that would follow later on will show that many things had happened. Horrible, awful things took place before I first informed Stojan Zupljanin about anything, and this is absolutely well known. If you take a look at the time-line of the events and also where these events were taking place, the first man in the investigation team, Vojin Bera, was trying to cover up -- he covered up the truth. He did not say that the consequences of the investigations that were conducted in Omarska and incidents in Omarska were such that some Bosniaks were dead. I believe I am clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Yes. But what's still a bit unclear to me is the information that, in the end, was passed on to Mr. Zupljanin. I understand that you tried to give to Mr. Zupljanin a true picture of what had happened at Omarska and Keraterm. So, at least from you, he would -- Mr. Zupljanin would eventually receive some information that would point to the true picture of what had happened. And then my question is: But what about all the others who also reported to Mr. Zupljanin, such as Vojin Bera and Simo Drljaca? Do you know if they were able to give a similar true picture of the situation in Omarska, Keraterm, and perhaps other camps; or did they all together seek to, as you said, hash it up.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, let me try once again to provide an answer to your question. Mr. Vojin Bera - I'm wrong again; he's just Vojin Bera - and Simo Drljaca, the two of them had much more information about these events than I did. I only spent one day in these camps; I mean, in Keraterm, in Omarska, and in Trnopolje. In this one single day, I saw something that I found to be awful and horrible, and I reported to Mr. Stojan Zupljanin about this in the presence of Djuro Bulic, Goran Sajnovic, and I already said what Djuro Bulic's comment about this was. He went away to play soccer, and he did not care about learning more about the things that I had noticed. However, now I'm in a position to say that somebody had probably checked what I had told Stojan Zupljanin. I suppose that, in connection with this, the commission also interviewed both Vojin Bera and Simo Drljaca. It probably received from them a picture that was quite different from what I had seen. The mayor of Banja Luka, Predrag Radic, told me on return from Prijedor that it was much worse than I had reported to the service. I do not know where he received this information from, what he was told about what I had said, but I do know for certain that I was not the only one who saw all this. Other members of the State Security Service and the public security service had seen the same, and it had been a trauma for them to spend any more time in Keraterm or in Omarska. I have mentioned one name, Obrad Despotovic. I could mention the names of other people who told me about incidents much worse than the ones I had witnessed. So, to conclude, if I may, and if you will allow that, after all that, I believe that Simo Drljaca, Vojin Bera, and others painted an untruthful picture of the events that were taking place in the area. They painted a picture that was much softer in terms of consequences. They were doctoring information, and they could have prevented the crimes which have been established in their number and nature in both Omarska and in Keraterm and in the general area of the Prijedor municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Back to you, Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: In connection with this question of His Honour Judge Harhoff, I will ask you something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see exhibit 2D02-0199 in e-court. It is tab 20 in the binder of Mr. Zupljanin's Defence. Could we please see the next page in the B/C/S version of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Have you talked about reports, and I will now show you one report. This is a report concerning the situation as found and questions relating to prisoners, collection centres, resettlement, and the role of the SJB in connection with these activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Could we please have a look at the page marked 0032542. That's the ERN number in the B/C/S version because this is a long document in e-court.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you just tell me whose report this is?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I will show you the last page and then you will see. Because you talked about reports which were sent. This is a report of a commission whose chairman was Vojin Bera, about whom you just talked. There are some other people who signed the report, because the subject was not just Prijedor, as you will see, but also Sanski Most and Bosanski Novi. And this is an amalgamated report about the situation requested by Mr. Stojan Zupljanin? First of all, do you recognise the signature of Mr. Vojin Bera?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. As for other signatures, I do not recognise these. But below the signatures I can see the names of these persons. I know Vaso Skondric and Jugoslav Rondic very well. As for the gentleman named Ranko Mijic [phoen], I don't know him so well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please go back to the first page of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: As can you see, what's discussed on the first page is the situation in the municipality of Prijedor. I don't know whether you've seen this document before. I don't believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But can we now please go to page 4 of the document where Omarska is discussed. That's in the B/C/S version, 0032-52530 [as interpreted]. The next page, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So the second paragraph from the top where conditions in Omarska are discussed.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please zoom in, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Zoom in the second paragraph which starts with the words: "Together with prisoners."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: But, in any case, you can read it, and I will summarise it for you. It's a new facility where a larger number of people can be accommodated. It involves drinking water, toilets, and such. And based on this report, we can see that it's exactly opposite and -- of the real situation and just as you told us, that this is a doctored report presenting things in a beautiful way.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me explain. It is correct that the facility has all -- all this that's mentioned, but the question was who was using these facilities. I can tell you that people who were there in detention or prisoners there did not use the showers. I know that for a fact. And that is the layer of veneer that covered up the rotting behind it. You have corroborated my belief that Mr. Zupljanin was exposed to lots of lies.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document into evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 2D90, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: We'll go back to the previous document.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please allow me to add just one more sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just want to give you my impression upon seeing this second paragraph on this page. I do not know what the reason was for such untruthful portraying of conditions, but the conditions as described by Vojin Bera and others remind me of what I have in this hotel called Ambassador here in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please put 2D25 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: This document, dated 30th of July -- first the Prosecutor showed you a video. Now, would you please take a look at the last page of the document. It's a document by the CSB sent to all SJBs, the command of the corps, and the operative duty officer. So the last page of the document, we can see the signature of Stojan Zupljanin. Now, let us go back to the first page, and we'll briefly go through it. You will find many sentences of yours in here. What we have here is a description of security situation and events that influence the situation in the centre. For instance, it's stated that because of war activities, what is pronounced is rebellion, and there's mention of paramilitary formations, the most serious crimes, and looting, ignoring the laws, illegal bearing of arms, and spreading of misinformation. There's mention of police members. It is stated that in some areas the situation is additionally complicated because of grave violations of the rules of service by the employees of the public security station who act illegally and do not abide by the measures that are within the competence of the organs of the interior. Furthermore, there's mention of criminal and antisocial phenomena. This has not seized, despite the fact that centre has drawn attention to the extent and harmfulness of such occurrences. Now, this is not trying to portray things in a pink -- with a pink shade. This is a realistic presentation of situation by Mr. Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And the Milos Group reported often about such situations. I do not wish to sound arrogant, but this is a compilation of a certain number of intelligence data collected on the ground by the Milos Group and myself. This is the first time that I get to see this text in toto. I can see to whom it was submitted, this report. The introductory part of this report and the second paragraph under it, the second paragraph I'd seen just a moment ago, I can tell you that the report really reflects the situation on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And when such events were noticed, it is necessary to have brought the support. That's why this was sent to several addresses because they were asking for assistance to resolve the problems existing on the ground.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, I'm sure you've understood me well. I specifically stressed that the report was sent to certain recipients, and that was done because I wanted to show the importance, both of the trends and to the attempts -- to find assistance that will lead the way out of the collapse. If I may just add one sentence. It may be of use to you. On the ground, it was not very clear. One could not distinguish easily because -- between black and white, right and wrong. During the entire period of 1992 and a part of 1993, many groups were present about whom nobody know -- nobody knew who they belonged to, even some of the local politicians, self-proclaimed or self-appointed politicians, people without any human dignity had their own groups maybe of their body-guards or just people working on promotion of the man's interest, so it would occasionally happen that when an operation needed to be done in relation to some members of one such group, we would get comments, Don't do it; they belong to you know who. And the local authorities were really powerful. They are more powerful than the authorities of today's state of Bosnia and Herzegovina are, both in relation to how the laws were implemented and in relation to taking care about citizens' freedom and so on. In some areas, there were people who were so powerful, not only in case of Mr. Simo Drljaca -- or I wish to correct myself. I'm saying Mr., Mr., but --

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Sorry. I apologise for interrupting. I don't think there's a question out there that he is answering. And given the limited time, I'm hoping that Defence counsel can keep it on track.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: After three days, counsel on both sides realise that they have to guide this witness. Please do so, Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Comrade Radulovic - and I apologise, I almost called you Mr. - but thank you for your explanation, yet you were saying not only Simo Drljaca, you meant in other municipalities as well. But we'll go through that through documents. If you could just confirm whether this is in keeping with what you know. And I apologise. I really started talking fast. Let us go back to the document. It is stated here that some of the active and reserve policemen have taken advantage of the wartime situation and participate in various criminal activities and illegally confiscate objects and property from citizens for themselves. This is something that you told us during your testimony on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us turn the page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: These kind of activities seriously damages the reputation of the profession and honorable and decent members of the service.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The problem was basically that a group of people who came to the police or who already worked for the police damaged the reputation of those members of the service who did their job honourably and decently.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Furthermore, it is stated that criminals very often in conducting their criminal activities were using uniforms and insignia of the Serbian army and the police.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: At the bottom of the page, we can see that some individuals in the police in their attempt to use the easier path close -- or turned their eyes away from such incidents. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the following page, please. Page 3 in the Serbian version where we can see that in the first paragraph, at the beginning, because there are fears related to information and in some cases because of the people's involvement in various criminal affairs, following the easier path, people do not carry out some of their duties, and the responsibility is very often something that they pass on to the centre. So --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Krgovic repeat his question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, I spoke very fast.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I will have to repeat the question. I really speeded up. So public security stations following this easier path failed to implement some orders they received from the centres. They covered up criminal activities, sometimes because they were themselves involved. And the responsibility, they tried to pass on to others and to the centre or shift to others and to the centre. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. We often discussed how the people committing crimes were justifying their actions by claiming that they received approval from the centre or maybe even Stojan Zupljanin. Before -- before this particular report, we had already written about it. You can check it in your documents. I believe that this report that we see is an attempt to make it known to everyone that such attempts should not and will not be tolerated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: In the second paragraph, it is stated that precisely because of such things there is fear among other people which leads to division between ethnic groups and mistrust of the institutions of the system. Furthermore, in the text, later in the text, Mr. Zupljanin points out that situation might get out of control which will have grave consequences for the security situation and the law and order, and that risk really existed. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. With all due respect, this report is something that is maybe up to 80 per cent compilation of information received by the Milos Group. I recognise the wording, terminology. I think this is a rather illustrative example of the situation on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: It also states here that -- you remember the sentence that you frequently mentioned, that this actually leads to the bitterness and indignation among the Serbian people in whose name and symbols these criminal acts are being committed.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Further down, Mr. Zupljanin is asking for measures to be taken to stem such conduct. And if you take a look at item 1 on that same page where he orders and states that the public security stations may carry out only jobs and tasks falling within their competence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now move on to page 4 in the Serbian. Page 4, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And then under item 2 it says: "Public security stations may not receive or carry out orders, decisions, conclusions, standpoints, et cetera, of crisis and regional staffs or other legal entities." I don't want to read the whole paragraph. But this is essentially what you have told us during your evidence here, that these matters were resolved at the levels of the police stations and that they were acting on orders from the local authorities. Correct?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And, in this manner, the functional unity of the service itself was being undermined?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. And in some cases even where you had town commands, these town commands would resubordinate public security stations and place them under their own authorities so that police stations literally reported to town commands and not to the ministry as they should according to the rules of service.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: That was the case in Skender Vakuf, in Kljuc, in Derventa specifically?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't want to waste any of -- more of your time. I will just answer with yes or no, and I will be as brief as I can. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Radulovic, did I understand correctly that when you used the term "town commands" you were referring to the Crisis Staffs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. No, Your Honours. In addition to Crisis Staffs, there was another body called the town command. And the town command had the powers -- or, rather, they arrogated the powers to place under their competence all armed units, for the purpose of defending the city or town, and all other activities that were linked to the -- or that had to do with the area where such a town command was established.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thanks. Do you know who established the town commands or how they were established?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were established with the approval of -- and the -- by the powers of the political authorities at the local level. And for this there was also the approval of the superior republic bodies or organs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Do you have any information about what the relations were between the Crisis Staffs and the town commands, where they existed in parallel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, you're asking my opinion. Of course --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will provide it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... please, Mr. Radulovic, if you don't know, then just say so, and we'll go on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would not be honest if I said that I didn't know. And that is why I said that I will answer your questions. There were very close links between them. And if I may add, Crisis Staffs were the ones who appointed commanders at the town commands, and they were in charge of all personnel issues -- or, rather, all personnel appointments in -- into such staff commands.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Town commands; interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Radulovic, would you now please take a look at items 9 and 10.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's on page 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Please take a look at paragraphs 9 and 10, which read: "You are to immediately take immediate, decisive, and uncompromising action to throw light on all criminal activities in public security stations and police stations, document them, and take appropriate legal measures of criminal misdemeanour, disciplinary, and material responsibility including temporary suspension and the measure of detention prescribed by the Law on Criminal Procedure and with the prior approval of the centre." This is precisely the order, if I may call it so, that you received from Mr. Zupljanin when you went to Teslic. Correct?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly. That is what -- this is how the work or the job was done in Teslic, in keeping with this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And then we see paragraph 10 where it says: "Deliver documented information, facts, and evidence, together with criminal reports, even against employees of public security stations to the competent public prosecutor. In cases where the public prosecutors are inactive, deliver criminal reports ... directly to the senior public prosecutor or the nearest public prosecutor. After taking measures against members of the active and reserve forces and removing them from the organ, immediately take them off wartime duty ..." And that's exactly what you did in Teslic. Correct?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And, again, in paragraph 7, it says: "Establish the existence and activity of paramilitary formations and inform the competent military security organs ..." And then it says: "Document the criminal activities of these units and individuals." That's exactly what did you in Teslic. Correct?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Now, in order to carry out these tasks and orders, it was necessary to launch a larger-scale action. And in some centres, as you said, there were certain difficulties, centres of public security stations, because they had actually -- they had actually split from the centre. Correct?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Now I will point out a portion of this document, and I am sure you will agree with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That will be in document Exhibit P621. That's the Prosecution's exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: This is a report on the work of Centre of Security Services, drafted by Stojan Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's in tab 4 of the Zupljanin folder. Page 20 -- or, rather, the ERN number is 0749643. I don't know if this is a good time for a break, or do you want me to go on?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: We're about three minutes early, but if this is convenient, I suppose we could take the break here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It's a convenient time, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I was reminded by Mr. Pantelic that Your Honours wanted our -- the position of Defence on the videolink.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And we do not object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Both Defences. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Radulovic, you see the document before you. And then I'm referring to the second paragraph, and I will read out the portion of it. And it says, in brief: "Inefficiency, lack of professionalism, and superficiality of work in a number of SJBs contributed to a large extent to the functional detachment of a number of SJBs from the centre. This has gratefully affected the overall unity and the social role of the security organs and services. Parallel to that, some of the SJBs connected themselves with the local politics and local political leaders, thereby neglecting their legal obligations and powers." In effect that was one of the greatest problems that you had in the area covered by your CSB in 1992. Correct?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And also, they reiterate here the conclusion about irresponsibility and political -- politique-ing. And then in the next paragraph, which confirm was you said today, it says: "It occurs on a quasi-regular basis that a number of the SJBs pay no attention to requests from the centre for information on certain issues, that is, there is no timely reaction to certain requests from the centre. This affects the unity and action capability of security organs and services as a unified security mechanism." In fact, this means that it was very difficult to control the overall security situation and to draw correct conclusions and assessments in the area because in order to do that you needed to have proper information; correct?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, of course. As in medicine, the right information that you get, as in medicine for diagnosing an illness that's already halfway healing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And, in fact - and you observed this too - this made it impossible for the centre to have the real picture of the situation on the ground because of such conduct by some of the SJBs; correct?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sorry 27, line 10, after the -- the answer "Yes," the rest of the -- that paragraph should be a question by Mr. Krgovic. After "Yes." That's 27, line 10.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] During the examination-in-chief -- I'll now move on to another topic. When the Prosecutor asked you whether you knew whether anything had been done in order to prevent incidents and some criminal acts by certain members of the SOS, you mentioned that had you some information from Mr. Zivko Bojic who told that you that there were some plans in that respect and that some action was taken but you didn't really know the details. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct. That's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to show you a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Exhibit 1D198. That's the Zupljanin folder, tab 13.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: This is an operative work-plan. Now, you remember that on a -- on the 12th of May you submitted some reports which indicated that there were certain criminal acts committed against Muslim small businesses where some hand grenades were placed or they were mined and so on. Now here we see the date of this operative work-plan is the 25th of May, 1992, for solving robberies, terrorism, extortion, et cetera, which have escalated in the territory of the Banja Luka SJB, all this being done by certain uniformed individuals and groups. And then mention is made of SOS, TO, Red Berets, and similar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please see page 5 of this document in the Serbian version.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: As you can see, we have the signature on the left-hand side. I believe that's Zivko Bojic's signature. That's what you are referring to; Correct?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And then on the right-hand side there is the signature of Mr. Zupljanin?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Now let's go back to page 2 of this document where these individuals are named, identified. And here mention is made of an individual that you mentioned when you spoke about those self-proclaimed dukes. There was this man called Palackovic, whose last name was Palackovic. Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know who this is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And then there is mention here of a Mercedes that was seized, and these people were -- these people engaged in stealing vehicles and throwing hand-grenades into houses. Now -- and some other individuals are mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, could we now go back to page 5 now for a moment. Page 5, please, where it says, in the fourth paragraph: "... these individuals were in a way self-organised ..." The fourth paragraph from the top in the Serbian version. Begins with the words: "In view of the fact that these individuals were in a way self-organised in the guise of membership of the SOS that they were well-armed and that some of them were mobilised by the JNA ..." It talks about these persons. And then in the following paragraph: "In order to ensure an efficient implementation of this plan, we need to have prior agreement with the regular and military courts on keeping all of the arrested persons in detention to present organised resistance. The reasons for detention exist for almost all of them." In essence, when this activity was planned, just like with the one in Teslic, a similar method was envisaged here. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, one might say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I will now show you the next document. This is 1D201. This is sometime later because time was necessary to implement the plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And this is tab 14 in the Zupljanin Defence folder.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object to where this line of questioning is going to lead. This witness has said that was he was aware that there was an operative plan, but he has no knowledge of whether it was ever carried out. And I believe the Defence now are going to try to show case files, of course, that this witness has never seen before, to try to convince him that that was -- that's wrong. And I'm not -- we're not going get anywhere with that information. And it's going to take up a lot of time. And I note that it's doubtful that witness has ever reviewed any of these case files so can really talk about what's contained in them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, whereas you can take the objection that Mr. Olmsted shouldn't anticipate you, isn't it apparent that he is correct in, as he says, it's something that's not going to assist us at the end of the exercise?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I just wish to refresh the witness's memory, if possible, as my learned friend would say, to present this document to him and to ask him whether any of the persons who are listed in this operative plan were, indeed, arrested. Just to see if the witness remembers that. Because a lot of time has passed. He was not specifically asked about these persons. I just wanted to ask him whether he knows whether they were -- there were criminal files filed against some of these persons and whether some of them were arrested or not. So that was just the substance of my --

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: The case files, Your Honour, speak for themselves. And they are admitted into evidence. And, you know, this is anecdotal evidence of something that -- we're not contending that these case files are unauthentic in any way; this witness simply is not going to have any information to add with regard to these case files. And if the Defence counsel has questions regarding these particular SOS members, he should just put the question to the witness; does he know what happened to particular members of the SOS or paramilitary groups, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, I was going to suggest exactly what Mr. Olmsted has just -- has just proposed. Just put the names to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that at one time, if you know, that, for example, Palackovic, Jungic, Kajkut, some of these persons whom you related to SOS were arrested and prosecuted?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not familiar that. I did not have this information. To be frank, I do not remember this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Because it was not your duty to follow what happened later on?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I will move to another subject now. During your testimony, you talked about the special unit attached to the Banja Luka CSB. Do you know that at one time, while the unit was still in the area of Kotor Varos, that for various reasons you mentioned, suggestions that you mentioned to Mr. Zupljanin, that they should be disbanded, that this detachment was indeed disbanded, and that the corps of this detachment came under the control of the army. And that was at some point in August 1992?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that there were certain transformations in place; however, I do not remember the time-line. And I also do not know what the actual motives for doing that were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Let me just show you briefly a document, 2D02-4204 [sic].

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 2D02-42 -- 0424. I apologise, I will repeat once again: 2D02-0424.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know Sreto Gajic?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: These are the minutes about his visit to the Security Services Centre in the month of July and in early August. Please have a look at the bottom. Point 1: "The special police detachment, 100 men strong, will be put at the disposal of the 1st Krajina Corps, under the command of General Talic, as of the 10th of August, 1992."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have a look at page 2 of this document now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The handover of the unit will be carried out at 0800 hours on the 10th of August, 1992, in Kotor Varos where the unit is deployed. The handover will be attended by Djuro Bulic, SJB sector chief on behalf of the CSB, and by Colonel Bogojevic, military security chief on behalf of the 1st Krajina Corps." Does that match the time when you heard that some transformation did take place?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I remember that it happened after the death of Colonel Stevilovic. He was replaced by Colonel Bogojevic. And I remember that the transformation took place at the time. However, I repeat that I don't know why this happened, what the motives were, because I just didn't deal with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And now that you've mentioned the death of Colonel Stevilovic, Stevan Markovic also killed at the same time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The death of these two men had a major impact on the security situation in the area because they were expert professionals, especially Colonel Stevilovic, together with whom you participated in some actions; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. I couldn't say who was a better man and a greater professional of these two. I couldn't give better attributes to one as opposed to the other. If I may just add, there was an idea at the level of the Security Services Centre and the 1st Krajina Corps and even wider that a mobile battalion should be set up. It should be a police battalion that would, in fact, resolve all incidents relating to the activities of renegade groups, or should I say criminals. They would, in fact, go wherever a problem arose. It would be very mobile. And this was an idea whose proponents and advocates were the late Stevan Markovic and the late Colonel Stevilovic, of course, together with the leadership of the then-Security Services Centre in Banja Luka. I believed that this was harmonised with the ministry or that somebody in the ministry had the same idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: When you talked about the activities of the special detachment, I will show now an exhibit, P591, a Prosecution Exhibit. We can see that this is the report from the army Main Staff, signed at the time by Mr. Tolimir. It's the Department for Intelligence and Security Affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see page 5 of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The date is the 28th of July, 1992. And on page 5, the then-Colonel Tolimir deals with the SOS, and he says: "The Serbian defence forces from Banja Luka SOS commanded by Stevandic, Nenad who is at the same time the president of the Serbian Falconers' Society. Private businessmen have much influence on the SOS and so do some officials from the SJB and SNB at the Banja Luka CSB." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a brief version, but it absolutely matches the information I had.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And then it says: "One part of the SOS, that's the SOJ, has been officially disbanded and became part of the establishment of the police detachment of the Banja Luka CSB, but it is not under actual control of the detachment and CSB command. One part of members have joined the Banja Luka TO, and another part headed by Branko Palackovic, and we talked about them, are now in detention." Was that how you saw this group, the mixture of the SOS and the special unit?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And now, just let me show you another document. And you might help us clarify something. When answering to a Prosecutor's question as you might remember, you talked about a report that had to do with the meeting with General Mladic in Teslic. The Prosecutor showed you the document that bears no date and which was found -- let me not say where because of the confidentiality of this document. And he asked you whether you remembered if the information was conveyed to Mr. Zupljanin. I will now show you another document which deals with this specific meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So if we could please see in e-court the exhibit 65 ter 871, which is marked as P1353.14. And let me just see what the tab number is. It's number 34. Tab 34 in our folder.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: This is a report dated the 30th of October, 1992. And if you have a look, these are operative workers, Radulovic, Stjepanovic, and Sajinovic, three operatives. It discusses the meeting. And please have a look who it was sent to.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: To the chief of the CSB and the chief of the SNB. When you discussed about the first document which is very similar, you said that it was talked at the meeting about replacing the leadership of the SNB and so on. I think that when you talked about which document you had sent to Mr. Zupljanin, I think that you had in mind this document which discusses the same incident but contains different information and different elements. And I think these were two different documents which were sent to different addresses. So if you can help us clarify this, please.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise for not answering immediately. I'm waiting for your question to be interpreted. But I can answer. I remember well this information. The information was very serious because it came from the man who, at the time, according to some of our assessments, enjoyed more respect than Radovan Karadzic himself. And what he said at the meeting was of great concern. We were surprised. And considering the seriousness of what we heard, and we heard it from a source that we absolutely trusted, we later even checked that, as I say, considering the weight of that, we did not introduce ourselves as members of the Milos Group. We, rather, said our first and last names so that we would show that personally we do not agree with such nonsense, regardless of who said that and where. If you wanted to refresh my memory, let me refresh your memory, that one of you told me, Was it possible that Mr. So-and-so said that. And I told you, Is it possible that Mr. So-and-so, that this information has to do with, said what he said in Srebrenica in public through a loud-speaker and in front of cameras. So I wanted to tell you that what is noted here is terrible. I also want to say that I could see from this the problems in which the state security and public security services were, because no one from these two services, with all due respect, including the accused, did not have such authority, such dignity, such references, so that any of them could be compared with the person who said this at the meeting in Teslic. And when such things are stated publicly and when fools get to hear that, you may as well imagine what kind of reaction you can expect on the ground. Because if someone tells you publicly that you can do whatever you want with non-Serbs and that you won't be held responsible for that, I think that that's a real disaster. I still think that today, I thought so at the time, and I shall always be of the same opinion. Speaking sincerely, I did not have much trust in the type of generals who came to the forefront at the time throughout Republika Srpska because, by contrast to other people, I know that they were a specific kind of generals. By that, I mean that they were not schooled regularly but they completed military academies in nine months. So I call them pregnant generals because this was the time of pregnancy. So to ridicule this we call them pregnant generals. Eventually it turned out that they really had been pregnant and that they give birth to something that was never to be found in the dignity and honour of the Serbian People.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And this document is your report?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's -- there's no doubt about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask for this document to be enter into evidence because it was not part of our package.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: This -- which ... are we talking about the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I understand it's already in.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: That's what I was about to say. The 30 October document is already in. We tendered it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And I do apologise. Just a correction. On the bottom left of the English version, we have two times chief of CSB, times one, so probably the other should be -- it's a typo. It should -- SNB, like State Security Service, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Radulovic -- or, rather, Comrade Radulovic, in relation to the situation in Banja Luka at the time and around that time, there were quite a few -- there were quite a few activities of the -- not only SNB and State Security Service but there was also a great presence of foreign intelligence services, including the Croatian one?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And as part of that, there were quite a lot of misinformation being placed, very often in relation to some of the leadership figures of Republika Srpska, both military and political.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And as part of that, it could occur that a National Security Service would get a piece of information that was planted and which would then leak out as factual information. It was very difficult, especially if the technical -- reliable technical means were used, and you, as part of the intelligence work that you conducted, you used the same methods, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, I see where you're going with this. You want to say that it -- there was a possibility that information received by Milos Group were not vary verified.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: No, no, no. I'm talking about a specific piece of information that was not discussed up until this moment. So I wasn't talking in general terms.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But let me just add one more word.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, go on.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I could accept what you just put, namely, your claim; but facts can confirm that we were almost invariably absolutely right. And let me complete my statement by saying that you're here talking about operative tricks, and, yes, it's true that intelligence services tried to trick each other. And, of course, it is possible that something was planted, some kind of information that was completely different to the actual state of affairs, and, in that respect, I agree with you, that such things could have happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: We have just agreed upon something, but I was not questioning the reliability of your information. We have seen that a lot of your formulations and wording found its way to the reports written by Mr. Zupljanin, but there was something else that was mentioned in passing by and is of great concern to our clients.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please repeat the number of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D37. It has to do with the evacuation from Kotor Varos.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, what -- in which binder, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Overlapping speakers] ... tab 40.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Zupljanin Defence binder.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, I should point out to you that you have exhausted the four and a half hours that you had requested. At what point do you expect you would be completed?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is the last topic I would like to present to the witness, and, therefore, in about five to ten minutes maybe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please see the following page of the document in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have only one page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Next page, please. Yes, that's the one. Can we please zoom in on the upper part of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: We've heard testimony here about who took part in the negotiations concerning the group leaving Vecici. What we can see here is -- are the minutes of the meeting of the Kotor Varos group. We can see here who were the persons who reached the decision concerning the transfer of the armed group and the evacuation of everyone from Vecici, both civilians and those who were armed. Let me repeat that Colonel Vogojevic [phoen], who took place of Colonel Stevilovic, informed the gathered people that he had been ordered by General Mladic that nobody should leave Vecici before all the armaments were surrendered. And then, further on, President Djekanovic from Kotor Varos says that there are differences between the position of Karadzic and the order issued by Mladic. Mayor Trivic then presented the views of the corps command, saying that nobody should leave before the -- all the weapons were handed in unconditionally and asked for the ultimatum to be repeated. Furthermore, he also stressed that President Djekanovic should, in his conversation with Karadzic, inform Karadzic that his position was not -- was something that is not -- has not been complied with and that he should inform Karadzic that unconditional surrender is the only solution.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's on the following page in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I'm not sure it was necessary for Mr. Krgovic to read the whole document, but it is -- I believe the last -- it's -- on the English, it is page 3, I think.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Krgovic also kindly read slowly. The interpreters can really not follow what he is reading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, did you hear the interpreter's comment?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Yeah, I heard it. I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From this document that is showing who the apartments were, at which level the decision was reached, and how the withdrawal was agreed upon, my client, Mr. Zupljanin, is saying that was in no way related to evacuation, that he didn't take part in any negotiations, that he wasn't present at the site of evacuation, and that the information that reached you, that himself and Colonel -- THE INTERPRETERS: Another colonel whose name the interpreters couldn't hear.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: -- and who also didn't take part in the negotiations were not in any way involved, that there was no mention of money. Would you -- would you accept such a claim?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I could accept such a claim easily. What I wanted to say was that the information wasn't something that we actually drafted and then submitted to either public or State Security Services. I told you - if I need to remind you - that that type of reports were drafted literally by - and I will give you a full name and surname - by Branko Ratic, who later became a head of Tajfun, which this -- this brought us into a situation which could all cost us our lives because that man was talking about all the most important political and other leaders of Republika Srpska. And he would then show a piece of footage saying, General Talic, that is something about you; General Mladic, this is what we have about you. And he would present that on the screen. And then one after the other in the same manner. I'm not sure whether Mr. Stojan Zupljanin found himself in such a situation with some kind of blackmail taking place. And then when those persons who went through this level of his complication --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat the last part of the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, Mr. Radulovic, the interpreters asked you to repeat the last part of your answer, please. They couldn't follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The witnesses didn't hear -- or, rather, the interpreters didn't hear the last part of your answer. Could you please start from the misinformation.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I will do my best, although ... What I was saying was that such kind of misinformation that was being sent to addresses of various consumers was something that was the end of us, because some of the individuals wanted to take their revenge on Branko Ratic for collecting such information. And then they saw that among the information there were reports by the Milos Group, and for that reason the members of the Milos Group also were being arrested, interrogated. And that was the reason why I was forced to leave the State Security Service of Republika Srpska, and so on and so forth, which is, all in all, something unnecessary for you. But I did want to say that precisely because of this method of operation by Tajfun, which may have been a patriotic way of work, but it was really not professional type of work, and it had overreaching ambitions, because Mr. Branko Ratic, and we're still friends today, wanted to be the number one security person in Republika Srpska. And I don't know what magic did he use, but, at one point, he did manage to get the ear of Radovan Karadzic to such a degree even that on several occasions, in my presence, he was establishing more direct contacts with Mr. Karadzic than I do with my wife after 35 years of marriage.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Of course, such misinformation could occasionally be used to have some people discharged for political games and that it could be used for very specific purposes, if politicians would use misinformation like this.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Viewing it from this vantage point in time, my opinion would be different from the one in -- I had in 1992 and 1993, yet I believe I should stress that among the information provided by Tajfun and forwarded by Branko Ratic, there were also accurate information. The only problem was that he did not hold the control mechanism in his hands, something to check up and verify his product. He was the last person in the chain of custody. He was the one handing in his reports to the top leadership members, very often reports based on unverified information. And now I'm coming to my point. Because of such way -- such activities of Tajfun, after realising that nobody's heeding what we are saying, nobody in Republika Srpska at least, we turned to Belgrade and asked for both Tajfun and Milos Group members to be called in and to ask our colleagues, professionals, from Serbia, in order to exert their influence and convince Tajfun to refrain from handing in their reports to institutions, organs, or important individuals in Republika Srpska, without their information first being verified and submitted to myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As the chief --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... could you remind me precisely where we are going.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the witness actually went outside my question, and he said that at one point Mr. Zupljanin did not forward the information, but I won't go into this anymore. I would just like to show a document that has to do with this: 1D03-3427. And that's my last question for this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: This is just to give the background for the misinformation surrounding Mr. Zupljanin. And please take a look at the document. It is a report from the 3rd of August, 1992, a meeting of the Assembly of the Autonomous Region of Krajina. And we see that there is here a certain number of members who were questioning or challenging the suitability of the members of the government. You must know -- I'm waiting for your answer to come -- to enter the transcript.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, is this your binder? I can't find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I apologise. This is Mr. Zecevic's binder, tab 85.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: The damage is already done, but we object to the question. It really just -- it's -- the question is about misinformation, and the counsel asked a question about a document. This is nothing about misinformation. And I think it's just really -- of course, he is entitled to ask leading questions, but suggesting, you know, theories to the witness is not the way to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I don't see what the problem is. Perhaps there is an misinterpretation of my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So, Witness, the misinformation that we mentioned earlier, that Mr. Zupljanin participated in negotiations and that they were paid for that --

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... that is not what the witness testified to. He didn't say that he was getting misinformation about Stojan Zupljanin's participation in the negotiations. This is, again, an example of Defence counsel twisting questions to put words into the witness's mouth.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, well, I will ask the witness directly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
